sections.h2: Where do Levy County owners pay and question property tax?
sections.html:
Levy owners pay at the Tax Collector's Bronson headquarters, 310 School Street, Suite 102 (352-486-5172), or at one of two branches. Valuation sits with a different office, the Property Appraiser, on the same street in Bronson at (352) 486-5222.

  • Bronson main office: 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson, FL 32621, Monday to Friday, opening 8:30 and closing 4:30
  • Williston branch: 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, FL 32696, (352) 528-6091.
  • Chiefland branch: 226 North Main Street, Chiefland, FL 32626, (352) 493-4646.

Address changes cannot be made at the collector's counter, for real property or tangible accounts alike; they go through the appraiser. A seller should update the mailing address there so a stray bill finds the right person after closing.

sections.h2: What are the Levy County property tax dates?
sections.html:
Bills fall due on November 1, and a balance still open after the following March 31 is delinquent from April 1. The state discount shrinks from 4 percent in November by one point per month to 1 percent in February.

Reminder letters on unpaid accounts go out by April 30. A delinquent list is prepared in May for the newspaper and the web, and the certificate auction usually runs by May 31, with Chapter 197 requiring a start no later than June 1.

Upstream of the bill, the state calendar is just as fixed: value as of January 1, exemption filings by March 1, a proposed-tax notice in August, and 25 days from that notice to petition on value.

sections.h2: How can you pay Levy County property tax online, and what does it cost?
sections.html:
Cards cost extra online and e-check does not. The collector's site lists 2.3 percent on credit cards, a flat $1.75 for charges below $76, and nothing for an online e-check (ACH); processor fees do not reach the county.

At the counter, every payment draws 2.3 percent and e-checks are unavailable. Anything processed after 11:59 p.m. counts as the next calendar day, a trap near a deadline. A seller wanting a clean payoff can use an online e-check before midnight to dodge both the fee and the next-day rule.

Cards accepted are Visa, Master Card, American Express and Discover. Call 352-486-5172 on a weekday if the system gives trouble.

sections.h2: What happens when Levy County property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent tax is sold off as a certificate, a lien instead of a transfer of the house. Its face amount stacks the unpaid tax, 1.5 percent a month for April and May, a 5 percent collector commission, the advertising charge and the cost of the sale.

Levy County tax certificate terms, from the Tax Collector's tax sale page
ItemAs the office prints it
Sale methodOnline auction through West Florida Business Systems, on or before May 31
Bid range0 to 18 percent in 0.25 percent steps, lowest rate wins
Minimum interest if redeemed on or after June 15 percent (not for zero bids)
Unbid certificatesIssued to the county at 18 percent
Certificate life7 years
Holder may seek a tax deedAfter two years from April 1 of the issuance year

The delinquent list runs weekly for three weeks ahead of the auction. Certificate buyers must wait two years, counting from April 1 of the issuance year, before contacting the owner.

sections.h2: What does a Levy County tax deed application involve?
sections.html:
An applicant files a signed form, redeems any other outstanding certificates, pays current tax if owed, and covers a $150 title search and a $75 application fee, amounts the office says can change without notice. The county clerk then schedules the sale and charges advertising, mailing and sheriff costs.

Where homestead is on the current roll, the opening bid adds half the assessed value to taxes and costs. A parcel nobody bids on can join the list of lands available for taxes, and land left unsold there for 3 years reverts to Levy County. Unpaid government liens survive a tax deed under s. 197.552.

Timing is the practical point for an owner planning to sell. Get a payoff figure from the collector for any certificate before listing, since a title company will want each lien cleared at closing.

sections.h2: What should Levy County sellers know about agricultural classification?
sections.html:
Farm classification stays with the seller, not the land. The appraiser's page calls it non-transferable, so a buyer files a fresh application after any sale or transfer.

Filing runs January 1 through March 1. Per the statute the office cites, only land used mainly for bona fide agriculture, meaning good-faith commercial use, qualifies. Zoning alone earns nothing, and the use should exist on the January 1 assessment date, or a reasonable effort to start it must have been made.

Selling acreage? Tell the buyer which parcels carry the classification now, because a buyer who fails to qualify may face a higher assessment. Denials are mailed to the applicant, who can ask the appraiser to talk it through.

sections.h2: How does the Levy County tax certificate auction treat bidders?
sections.html:
The sale runs online through West Florida Business Systems, and the Tax Collector says no deposits are required for the current format. Every bidder must submit a Participating Bidder Agreement after registering or logging in, plus an electronic W-9 each year.

The office also runs a test system so new bidders can practice, and bids made there do not carry over to the live sale. A certificate can be sold to another buyer if the endorsement form and a transfer fee of $2.25 per certificate reach the Tax Collector. The office warns that a certificate is not a guaranteed investment, and if no action is taken within the seven-year life while the tax stays unpaid, the certificate is cancelled. For an owner, this means the lien is held by a private investor who is barred from contacting you for the first two years but who may then apply for a deed.

sections.h2: Who lives in Levy County, and what do homes cost?
sections.html:
Levy County is rural: about 48,520 people live across 1,118 square miles, roughly 38 per square mile in the 2020 count, and the population has risen 13.1 percent since then.

Census data for 2020 to 2024 give an owner-occupied home a median value of $190,600, with 81.4 percent of 22,192 housing units lived in by owners, rent at $850 and household income at $56,750. Households number 18,562 at 2.43 people each, the median selected monthly owner cost with a mortgage is $1,297 and without one is $375, and only 16.5 percent of adults hold a bachelor's degree. Broadband subscriptions reach 80.8 percent of households, workers average a 30.4 minute commute, and builders pulled 244 permits in 2025. People 65 and over are 26.7 percent of the county, and 91.1 percent of residents stayed put in the previous year. Long tenure usually means a Save Our Homes assessment below market, which resets after a sale.

A Levy County deed carries Florida's 70 cents per $100 stamp tax, paid to the clerk at recording by whichever party the deal assigns, with every party liable.

faqs.q: Where is the Levy County Tax Collector?
faqs.a: Headquarters: 310 School Street, Suite 102, Bronson. Branches: 551 SW 1st Avenue, Williston, and 226 North Main Street, Chiefland. All keep weekday hours.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay Levy County property tax online?
faqs.a: Cards add 2.3 percent, or $1.75 flat under $76, payable to the processor. Online e-checks cost nothing; office payments add 2.3 percent.

faqs.q: When does Levy County property tax become delinquent?
faqs.a: From April 1 following the bill. Reminders mail by April 30 and the certificate auction normally closes out by May 31.

faqs.q: Can a buyer keep my Levy County agricultural classification?
faqs.a: No, the appraiser calls it non-transferable. A buyer needs a new application by March 1 and must pass the bona fide agriculture test.

faqs.q: How soon can a tax deed be sought on unpaid Levy County tax?
faqs.a: Two years after the April 1 of the issuance year, a certificate holder may apply. If one exists on your parcel, request a payoff figure from the collector.
